   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.

   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)

     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Empirical analysis covers municipal water service delivery across Portugal using data from the Portuguese Water Sector Regulator (ERSAR).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 4, Section 4 and Section 4.1

effect_estimate.comment: One-way ANOVA and bivariate correlation results across 308 Portuguese municipalities in 2009 show that organizational costs have the strongest relationship with user prices, while private PPP concessions exhibit higher user prices and more user complaints than public bureaucracies and municipal corporations, alongside slightly higher compliance with water quality standards for human consumption.
effect_estimate.value: Organizational costs had the strongest effect on domestic water user prices across all consumption levels (60 m3: F = 264.761, p = .000, eta^2 = .723, r = .829; 120 m3: F = 124.198, p = .000, eta^2 = .551, r = .699; 180 m3: F = 58.669, p = .000, eta^2 = .367, r = .542), with private property showing higher mean organizational costs (EUR 43.20) than public property (EUR 20.07). Private property had significantly higher user prices than public property (60 m3: F = 66.313, p = .000, eta^2 = .178, private M = EUR 78 vs. public M = EUR 44; 120 m3: F = 52.359, p = .000, eta^2 = .146, M = EUR 129 vs. EUR 83; 180 m3: F = 42.319, p = .000, eta^2 = .121, M = EUR 201 vs. EUR 136), more user complaints (F = 22.682, p = .000, eta^2 = .071; private M = 34 vs. public M = 6), slightly higher parametric water quality compliance for human consumption (PaV: F = 7.877, p = .005, eta^2 = .026; private M = 99.2% vs. public M = 97.8%), and no difference in required parametric test completion (PaT: F = 0.728, p = .394, eta^2 = .002). Management model also significantly differentiated user prices (60 m3: F = 29.562, p = .000, eta^2 = .281; bureaucracy M = EUR 40, municipal corporations M = EUR 54, private firms M = EUR 76) and complaints (F = 16.642, p = .000, eta^2 = .186; bureaucracy M = 1, municipal corporations M = 17, private firms M = 36).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 6-8, Section 5; Tables 2-5, PDF pp. 6-8

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional observational design (ceiling = 2) documenting statistical associations (ANOVA and Pearson correlations) between institutional ownership/management models, organizational cost structures, user tariffs, complaints, and water quality across municipalities; specific contractual and cost-internalization mechanisms (e.g., town-hall cost sharing, Decree-Law 194/2009, concession risk/penalty clauses) are invoked from legal texts and secondary literature rather than directly observed in primary administrative process data.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 5-8, Sections 4.3-6

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines domestic water tariffs/user fees and statutory cost internalization into tariffs (fees), user complaints tracked by the regulator ERSAR to resolve operator-user problems (complaint), contractual/regulatory financial penalties and rescission for quality deviations or non-reporting (sanction), and municipal-operator tariff negotiations, political appointment/contracting of corporate boards, and departmental cost-sharing (political_coordination). Note: the paper's variable 'property' refers to public vs. private utility ownership rather than household land/property eligibility.
